meals.title: Chicken Bouillabaisse

ingredients.note: halved from 1/4 tsp for low heat

meals.notes: Loved redo (5 stars, Oct). Pool day: brown the chicken, build the saffron-fennel broth, nestle the thighs on the potatoes skin-up, oven 375°F, then broil to crisp; cool and refrigerate. At dinner reheat covered at 350°F and broil a few minutes to re-crisp the skin. 6 servings: Sunday dinner for two, his Mon + Tue lunches, and 2 to freeze for later lunches (frozen is lunch-only). Seafood-free despite the name. No rouille or toasts this time (dropped 11/21); the potatoes in the pot are the carb. Skim the fat (heart-health). Lower-sodium build (2026-11-21): no added salt (to taste = Jami's table salt), no-salt-added tomatoes; lean on the saffron, orange zest, pastis and a squeeze of lemon at the table. Salted light: Jami, salt at the table.

nutrition.servingDescription: 1 1/3 thighs (one large or two small) with about 1 1/2 cups broth, potatoes and fennel
assumptions: 3 lb bone-in thighs yield about 2.4 lb meat and skin; skin is eaten (it is crisped)
about a third of the chicken fat and half the oil renders out and is skimmed
about a third of the wine and ouzo alcohol calories remain after the oven braise
low-sodium broth at 140 mg per cup; no-salt-added diced tomatoes, drained
no added salt: the recipe salts to taste, and to taste means Jami salts at the table (rule from 2026-11-21)

meals.title: Whole Roasted Snapper with Citrus Vinaigrette

ingredients.note: 1 1/2 to 2 lb, scaled and gutted (half the book recipe). Alt: whole branzino or sea bass (book), or skin-on snapper fillets roasted about 10 min
a tiny pinch, or skip (book: 1/8 tsp for 4)
in the citrus-zest rub (book: 3/4 tsp table salt per fish); none extra in the vinaigrette

meals.notes: Fresh fish for two, cooked and eaten (buy it Sunday). Oven 500°F, parchment-lined sheet. Whisk the vinaigrette (oil, cilantro, lime and orange juice, shallot, pepper flakes). Mix the lime and orange zest with the salt and pepper; slash the skin, rub the zest-salt inside and out, let sit 10 min. Roast 15-20 min to 140°F; rest 5 min, fillet with two cuts and lift off the bones; spoon the vinaigrette over. Avoid fish over 2 lb. Salted light: Jami, salt at the table.

nutrition.servingDescription: half a whole snapper, about 6 oz of fish, with 1 1/2 tbsp citrus vinaigrette
assumptions: a 1 3/4 lb whole snapper gives about 12 oz of raw fillet
1/2 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher in the zest rub; about 70% eaten (some stays on skin and bones)
about 2 1/2 of the 3 tbsp oil end up eaten in the vinaigrette

meals.title: Herbed Barley Pilaf
meals.notes: Half batch: Monday dinner for two plus one lunch. Soften the onion in the oil with the salt, add barley, garlic and thyme, toast 3 min; add the water, simmer covered on low until tender and absorbed, 20-40 min. Off heat, towel under the lid 10 min; fold in parsley, chives and lemon. Whole grain for the LDL. Salted light: Jami, salt at the table.

assumptions: 3/4 cup dry pearl barley makes about 3 cups cooked
1/4 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher in total (halved)

meals.notes: Half batch: Monday dinner plus a lunch. Braised with tomato, coriander and paprika, finished with lemon and parsley; it holds well in the fridge. No salt in the pot: the recipe salts to taste, so Jami salts at the table.

meals.title: Greek Style Stuffed Peppers

ingredients.note: canned, drained and rinsed (regular canned, rinsed, adds about 50 mg per pepper)
for the baking dish (instead of broth)

meals.notes: One-dish full meal (beef, rice, peppers), dairy-free. Soak the rice 20-30 min while you chop. Brown onion then beef deeply; add parsley, rice, paprika, tomato sauce + 2 1/4 cups water, simmer to half, then low and covered 20 min. Meanwhile char the peppers on a grill pan or skillet 10-15 min, covered, turning. Stuff, set in a dish with 3/4 cup broth/water, foil-tent, 350°F for 20-30 min. 6 peppers: Tue dinner for two, his Wed lunch, Wed dinner for two, 1 to freeze for a lunch. Freezes 1-2 months; reheat in a medium oven with a splash of liquid. Red meat night of the week (1/2 lb across 6 = lean). Wednesday dinner is the leftovers: reheat covered at 350°F with a splash of water, ~20 min. Lower-sodium build (2026-11-21): no added salt (to taste = Jami's table salt), no-salt-added tomato sauce and chickpeas, water in the baking dish; finish with lemon. Salted light: Jami, salt at the table.

assumptions: no-salt-added tomato sauce and chickpeas; water, not broth, in the baking dish
cross-check: The Mediterranean Dish publishes 270 kcal and 196 mg sodium per pepper; calories agree and sodium is now a little lower
no added salt: the recipe salts to taste, so Jami salts at the table

meals.title: Grilled Duck Breasts in Cherry-Port Sauce
meals.source: Meathead: The Science of Great Barbecue and Grilling — p.315

ingredients.note: "plump" (book: 2 breasts = 2 servings; 1 per person). Hard to find: Whole Foods / Bristol Farms / Gelson's, or frozen at Asian markets
dried sage, parsley, rosemary, thyme, oregano, basil, bay, black pepper, sugar, pulsed coarse; make a pinch-batch at home
2 for the shallots, 2 to mount the sauce
book: balsamic (or raspberry vinegar); his menu uses red wine vinegar
book: dried cherries; sour per his menu. Alt: dried cranberries or raisins (book notes)
a few sprigs in the sauce, per his menu (not in the book recipe)
dry brine for both breasts (about 1 lb): Meathead's 1/2 tsp per pound

meals.notes: Scaled for 2 (book makes 2). Score the skin in a 3/4-1 in crosshatch through the fat, salt + rub both sides, dry brine ~3 hr. Book method: two-zone grill, cast-iron pan preheated on the hot side 10 min; skin side down until dark brown, flip and sear 3 min, move breasts to the indirect side to 135°F (~30 min). Sauce in the wiped pan: 2 tbsp butter, shallots till limp, then broth, port, vinegar and cherries reduced by half; mount with 2 tbsp butter. Slice thin on an angle, fan over sauce. No grill at the rental: render skin-side down over medium in cast iron (pour off fat as it builds), flip and sear 3 min, finish in a 300–325°F oven to 135°F; vent the kitchen, it smokes. Save the clean duck fat for potatoes.

nutrition.servingDescription: 1 duck breast, sliced, with about 1/3 cup cherry-port sauce
assumptions: Pekin breast lobes of about 8 oz raw each; a larger Moulard magret would add roughly 50%
scored skin renders out about 60% of its fat, poured off
8 oz sweetened dried tart cherries makes a lot of sauce; about three-quarters of it assumed eaten
about 40% of the port's alcohol calories remain after reducing
dry brine is Meathead's 1/2 tsp Morton kosher per pound, about 1 lb of duck, about 80% retained

meals.title: Roasted Delicata Squash with Brown Butter, Crispy Sage, and Hazelnuts

Meanwhile brown the butter over medium until the foam subsides, add sage ~30 sec until the butter is light hazelnut-brown and the sage crisp; pour over the squash immediately, toss, top with toasted hazelnuts. Toast/chop hazelnuts at home Wednesday.

meals.title: Pear Tarte Tatin

ingredients.note: firm, slightly underripe; halve and pack in as many as fit the 10-in skillet (they shrink). FN calls for 12-15 underripe Anjou
10-11 in; larger than the pan. Dufour (Whole Foods) or Trader Joe's seasonal all-butter
his menu adds butter to the caramel; stir in off the heat once it turns golden (not in the FN recipe)

meals.notes: FN method: 400°F. CLEAN 10-in cast-iron skillet; 3/4 cup sugar + 3 tbsp water over medium-low, swirl, don't stir, until golden, 10-12 min. Off heat, pack in the pear halves (crowd them; they shrink). Back on low ~20 min until the fruit soaks up the caramel. Drape the puff pastry over, tuck the edges, cut three 2-in slits. Bake 40-45 min until browned and the pears are tender. Cool only 10-15 min, pour off and reserve excess caramel, flip onto a platter, pour the caramel back, push loose fruit into place. Serve with vanilla ice cream. (Skipping the recipe's optional cranberry caramel.) Tips: firm, slightly underripe pears; clean utensils or the caramel goes grainy. Bake it in the cast-iron skillet he's bringing. It serves 8–10, so there's tart for Friday breakfast too.

nutrition.servingDescription: 1/8 of the tart with a 1/4-cup scoop of vanilla ice cream
assumptions: about 75% of a 14 oz all-butter puff pastry sheet is used after trimming
8 Bosc pears, peeled and cored (about 85% edible)
all the caramel is poured back over the tart
1 pint regular vanilla ice cream split over 8 servings

ingredients.note: about 12 oz; pick unenhanced (no added broth or salt solution). Half the recipe
bring a pinch from home; alt: dried thyme + oregano + a few sesame seeds. Store blends often contain salt
skip, or a pinch on your plate (book: 1/2 tsp for 4)
the carb; cook per the box in water, no salt
on the chicken only (the recipe's measured seasoning, halved); the sauce's to-taste pinches are left to Jami at the table

meals.notes: Rainy-night backup in Joshua Tree, if you don't eat out: everything from the Vons there plus a small kit from home, all stovetop in your cast iron (no grill or oven needed). Mix half the za'atar with the paprika and garlic powder; season the thighs with it and the salt. Soften the sliced onion in oil, push aside, sear the thighs 4-5 min a side; add the cherry tomatoes, lemon juice and the rest of the za'atar, cover 5-10 min until the tomatoes burst and the chicken hits 165°F. Finish with oil, lemon zest and parsley. Serve over whole-wheat couscous. Salted light: 1/4 tsp on the chicken only; Jami salts at the table.

assumptions: 3 boneless skinless thighs, about 4 oz each raw, unenhanced
1/4 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher on the chicken only; no to-taste salt in the sauce
za'atar without added salt (a salted store blend adds about 100-200 mg)
2/3 cup dry whole-wheat couscous cooked without salt

meals.title: Snow White Roll (Wazabi Sushi takeout)
meals.notes: Jami's out and he doesn't cook just for himself, so it's his go-to: the Snow White roll on its own (no rice; tuna, salmon, yellowtail, crab salad, spring mix, mango and avocado in soy paper, topped with sesame dressing, chili oil and ponzu). His order: no ponzu, no sesame dressing and none of the brown sauce at the bottom; keep the chili oil (it's mostly oil and chile, little sodium). No dipping soy sauce. Keep breakfast and lunch low-sodium that day. Lunch can be a freezer portion (daube or Spanish chicken).

assumptions: restaurant portions: about 1 1/2 oz each of tuna, salmon and yellowtail
crab salad is imitation crab with about 1 tbsp mayo
ordered with chili oil only: no ponzu, sesame dressing or brown sauce (those add about 700 mg); about 1 tsp chili oil, unsalted
no dipping soy sauce
